# PowerShell and C# API parity

I use the same domain names for cmdlet parameters, C# configuration and fluent calls. PowerShell keeps numeric duration parameters with units and default-off switches; C# keeps TimeSpan values and Boolean properties.

The contract covers **89 commands**, **1034 parameters** and **317 reachable public types**. The metadata gate checks names, types, sets, positions, defaults, nullability and member paths. Rendering and triplet tests check behavior.

Table and List remain named shortcuts to Show-Console’s shared view implementation. Read-* returns answers; New-ConsoleForm/Menu defines a question workflow; Show-ConsoleApp runs a persistent reactive application.

Typed Options on export, form, menu and replay operations expose the corresponding C# configuration. I can pass a PowerShell hashtable, for example `Export-ConsoleFrame -Format Html -Options @{ Width = 100; Padding = 8 }`. Options and individual settings are mutually exclusive; the supplied request is not modified.

Callback properties use `.Configure(item => item.Action = …)`. C# invokes a delegate-valued property before considering an extension with that name; Configure assigns the callback without invoking it.

## Fluent construction and nesting

Ui is the fluent entry point: New-ConsolePanel becomes Ui.Panel(), named settings stay in the chain, and nested Content uses c.Panel(p => …). Initializers retain constructors. Factories accept no positional configuration; the recorded primary inputs below are the only exceptions. Chart, Progress and kind-selected inputs materialize their existing typed options through the shared Build operation.

Literal text uses `Ui.Text(text)` or `c.Text(text)`; PowerShell `-Markup` uses `Ui.Markup(markup)` or `c.Markup(markup)`. Boolean properties named IsX keep that property in initializers and use `.X()` / `.X(false)` in fluent chains. Adjacent configuration stays in one chain.

Operation options use a typed configure callback, for example `ConsoleRun.ForEachAsync(items, work, o => o.ThrottleLimit(2).Title("Build"))`. The operation creates fresh defaults, invokes the callback once and delegates to its existing implementation. `Ui.Options<T>()` is removed.

## Parameter-set mappings

A structural parameter set can select a different request model. The metadata gate checks these mappings separately and includes both update requests in its public-member coverage.

| Command and parameter | Set | C# member | Conversion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `New-ConsoleTable -InputObject` | Live | `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.LiveTable.Set` | Live rows retain a stable key and projected values; model reuse adapts input records through the same keyed Set operation. |
| `Update-Console -Detail` | Run | `ConsoleMonster.Live.RunUpdate.Detail` | Identity |
| `Update-Console -Index` | Run | `ConsoleMonster.Live.RunUpdate.Index` | Run requires exactly one index; the cmdlet rejects zero or several elements before using the sole scalar position. |
| `Update-Console -Label` | Run | `ConsoleMonster.Live.RunUpdate.Label` | Identity |
| `Update-Console -Status` | Run | `ConsoleMonster.Live.RunUpdate.Status` | Identity |
## Individual member decisions

Native host hooks, runtime models and equivalent representations are listed individually. These decisions do not exempt a namespace or hide newly added options.

| C# member | Disposition and reason | PowerShell route or alternative |

| `ConsoleMonster.Changes.ChangePreviewOptions.Interactive` | CSharpOnly: The PowerShell adapter supplies its own prompt devices and runspace; C# embedding hosts can provide different devices. | Compare-ConsoleObject uses the owning PowerShell host for confirmation. |

| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Legend.Entries` | CSharpOnly: Legend entries describe the application-supplied meanings of an explicit view. | Populate Legend.Entries and pass the widget to Show-Console. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.AdditionalLegendEntries` | CSharpOnly: Extra legend words describe application-supplied matrix annotations. | Populate Matrix.AdditionalLegendEntries before passing the matrix to Show-Console. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.CellNote` | CSharpOnly: A cell annotation describes the supplied matrix values. | Set Matrix.CellNote before passing the matrix to Show-Console. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.InlineAxes` | CSharpOnly: Inline axes are an explicit matrix presentation choice. | Set Matrix.InlineAxes before passing the matrix to Show-Console. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.LegendRoles` | CSharpOnly: Legend tones belong to the application-supplied matrix status meanings. | Populate Matrix.LegendRoles before passing the matrix to Show-Console. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.MinCellWidth` | CSharpOnly: The minimum matrix cell width is a native layout constraint. | Set Matrix.MinCellWidth before passing the matrix to Show-Console. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.ShortColumnAxisCaption` | CSharpOnly: A compact column caption is supplied independently of the full matrix caption. | Set Matrix.ShortColumnAxisCaption with ColumnAxisCaption on a native Matrix. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.ShortRowAxisCaption` | CSharpOnly: A compact row caption is supplied independently of the full matrix caption. | Set Matrix.ShortRowAxisCaption with RowAxisCaption on a native Matrix. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.ShowLegendCounts` | CSharpOnly: Legend counts are an explicit matrix summary presentation choice. | Set Matrix.ShowLegendCounts before passing the matrix to Show-Console. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.PathHop.Bold` | CSharpOnly: Emphasis belongs to an explicitly supplied native path hop. | Set PathHop.Bold on a hop in a PathSet before passing the widget to Show-Console. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.PathHop.Role` | CSharpOnly: A hop tone expresses application-supplied relationship meaning. | Set PathHop.Role on a hop in a PathSet before passing the widget to Show-Console. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.PathSet.CompactBranches` | CSharpOnly: Compact connectors are an explicit native path layout choice. | Set PathSet.CompactBranches before passing the widget to Show-Console. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ScoreGauge.Maximum` | CSharpOnly: The gauge maximum is supplied by the application alongside its score. | Set ScoreGauge.Maximum and pass the gauge to Show-Console. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ScoreGauge.Parts` | CSharpOnly: Score components are labels and values supplied by the application. | Populate ScoreGauge.Parts and pass the gauge to Show-Console. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ScoreGauge.Role` | CSharpOnly: The finding tone is supplied by the application rather than computed by the gauge. | Set ScoreGauge.Role and pass the gauge to Show-Console. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ScoreGauge.Value` | CSharpOnly: The gauge displays an application-supplied score without calculating it. | Set ScoreGauge.Value and pass the gauge to Show-Console. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ScoreGauge.Width` | CSharpOnly: A fixed gauge width is an explicit native layout choice. | Set ScoreGauge.Width and pass the gauge to Show-Console. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TableRowRole.MarkerTone` | CSharpOnly: A row marker tone is supplied independently of the row label and status. | Set MarkerTone on a native TableRowRole used by the table builder. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Tree.CompactGuides` | CSharpOnly: Compact guides are an explicit native hierarchy layout choice. | Set CompactGuides on the Tree returned by New-ConsoleTree before passing it to Show-Console. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Tree.ValuePlacement` | CSharpOnly: Value placement selects the layout of explicitly supplied tree value columns. | Set ValuePlacement on the Tree returned by New-ConsoleTree before passing it to Show-Console. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TextBlock.WrapSeparator` | CSharpOnly: Separator-aware wrapping is a layout option on an explicit TextBlock; New-ConsoleText returns RichText and does not expose this option. | Construct a TextBlock, set WrapSeparator, and pass the widget to Show-Console or use it as a ConsoleViewFrame footer. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TreeNode.MeasureBareLabel` | CSharpOnly: This per-node option includes a bare node in measurement of explicitly configured tree value columns. | Set MeasureBareLabel on a bare TreeNode in an explicit tree with ValueColumns, then pass the tree to Show-Console. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TreeNode.Bare` | CSharpOnly: A bare node omits the ordinary hierarchy decoration in an explicit tree. | Set Bare on a native TreeNode before passing its tree to Show-Console. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TreeNode.TruncateLabelInMiddle` | CSharpOnly: Preserving both ends of one node label is a per-node layout choice. | Set TruncateLabelInMiddle on a native TreeNode before passing its tree to Show-Console. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ViewHeader.Facts` | CSharpOnly: Header facts are supplied by an embedded view builder. | Populate ViewHeader.Facts and pass the header or its ConsoleViewFrame to Show-Console. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ViewHeader.State` | CSharpOnly: The header state is supplied by the application and can contain status markup. | Set ViewHeader.State and pass the header or its ConsoleViewFrame to Show-Console. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ViewHeader.Streaming` | CSharpOnly: An open-stream header describes collection rather than a final verdict. | Set ViewHeader.Streaming in a native streaming-header builder. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ViewHeader.Title` | CSharpOnly: The embedded view title is literal application-supplied context. | Set ViewHeader.Title and pass the header or its ConsoleViewFrame to Show-Console. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ViewHint.Columns` | CSharpOnly: Hidden column names are supplied by the view layout owner. | Populate ViewHint.Columns and use the hint as a native view footer. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ViewHint.MoreRows` | CSharpOnly: The omitted-row count is supplied by the view collection owner. | Set ViewHint.MoreRows and use the hint as a native view footer. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Export.ExportOptions.ColorDepth` | CSharpOnly: Export rendering creates its own fixed profile from ColorDepth; the cmdlet deliberately keeps TrueColor rather than inheriting the terminal target depth. | Use Export-ConsoleFrame for its normal artifact profile; native exporters can set ExportOptions.ColorDepth explicitly. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Export.ExportOptions.Culture` | CSharpOnly: A native artifact renderer can pin numeric/date culture independently of its host; the cmdlet leaves Culture null and uses the current culture. | Select the PowerShell current culture before rendering, or set ExportOptions.Culture in native export code. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Export.ExportOptions.DarkTheme` | CSharpOnly: Native HTML/SVG callers may inject a custom dark ITheme; the cmdlet exposes only the ExportTheme preset selector and leaves the custom theme unset. | Use Export-ConsoleFrame -Theme Auto/Dark/Light/HighContrast; supply DarkTheme through native ExportOptions for custom palettes. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Export.ExportOptions.Elapsed` | CSharpOnly: A native snapshot renderer can pin the session clock for spinners and header clocks; fresh widget exports keep the zero-time default. | Export a captured frame/session for its rendered state, or set ExportOptions.Elapsed in a deterministic native renderer. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Export.ExportOptions.Fragment` | CSharpOnly: HTML embedding hosts can request a styled fragment rather than a complete page; Export-ConsoleFrame produces its self-contained document contract. | Consume the full HTML from Export-ConsoleFrame -Format Html, or request Fragment in a native HTML exporter. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Export.ExportOptions.Glyphs` | CSharpOnly: Export rendering uses the option's Full glyph tier independently of the ambient terminal target; the cmdlet keeps that artifact default. | Use Export-ConsoleFrame with full export glyphs, or configure ExportOptions.Glyphs in a native exporter. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Export.ExportOptions.IndividualTextElements` | CSharpOnly: Native SVG consumers with limited text models can request one element per grapheme; ordinary SVG export keeps compact text and the graphics provider selects its required representation internally. | Use Export-ConsoleFrame -Format Svg/Png for the supported serializers; native SVG integration can set IndividualTextElements. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Export.ExportOptions.LightTheme` | CSharpOnly: Native dual-theme exports may inject a separate light ITheme; the cmdlet keeps the built-in light palette instead of an arbitrary theme object. | Use Export-ConsoleFrame -Theme Auto or Light; native ExportOptions.LightTheme supports a custom light palette. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Export.ExportOptions.LineHeight` | CSharpOnly: Native artifact hosts can alter the font-to-cell-height ratio; the cmdlet keeps the 1.2 geometry while exposing font size and cell dimensions. | Use Export-ConsoleFrame -FontSize/-Width/-Height; set LineHeight in native ExportOptions for custom cell metrics. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Export.ExportOptions.Padding` | CSharpOnly: Native page/image embedding can set its pixel margin; the cmdlet keeps the 12-pixel frame margin and lets raster presets choose their composition. | Use Export-ConsoleFrame -Preset for the supported raster composition, or set ExportOptions.Padding in native embedding code. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Export.RecordingExportOptions.Culture` | CSharpOnly: Native recording renders may pin numeric/date culture; PlaybackOptions leaves Culture null and uses the current culture. | Select the PowerShell current culture before exporting, or supply RecordingExportOptions.Culture from a native renderer. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Export.RecordingExportOptions.CustomTheme` | CSharpOnly: Native recording exporters can supply one custom ITheme; the cmdlet deliberately accepts the built-in Theme presets and leaves CustomTheme unset. | Use Export-ConsoleRecording -Theme Dark/Light/HighContrast, or native RecordingExportOptions.CustomTheme for an injected palette. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Export.RecordingExportOptions.FontSize` | CSharpOnly: Native recording serializers can set natural-size typography; the cmdlet keeps the 14-pixel recording font. MaxFontSize is a raster fitting ceiling, not this setting. | Use Export-ConsoleRecording -Preset/-MaxFontSize for raster fitting; configure FontSize in native recording export options for natural-size typography. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Export.RecordingExportOptions.Glyphs` | CSharpOnly: Native recording rendering can choose a glyph tier; the cmdlet keeps Full glyphs rather than exposing another artifact-profile override. | Use the standard Export-ConsoleRecording artifact profile, or set RecordingExportOptions.Glyphs in native export code. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Export.RecordingExportOptions.LineHeight` | CSharpOnly: Native recording serializers can alter the cell-height multiplier; the cmdlet retains the shared 1.2 geometry. | Use the supported recording dimensions and raster presets; native RecordingExportOptions.LineHeight controls custom cell metrics. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Export.RecordingExportOptions.Loop` | CSharpOnly: This Boolean controls SVG animation repetition. The cmdlet keeps SVG looping enabled; LoopCount controls the separate GIF/APNG graphics job and is not this property. | Use Export-ConsoleRecording -LoopCount for raster animation; set RecordingExportOptions.Loop for native SVG repetition policy. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Export.RecordingExportOptions.MaxFrames` | CSharpOnly: This is the export sampler's regular-frame cap of 900; Show-ConsoleReplay -MaxFrames governs the different in-terminal player job. | Use Export-ConsoleRecording -FramesPerSecond for export sampling frequency; native RecordingExportOptions.MaxFrames controls the export cap. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Export.RecordingExportOptions.Padding` | CSharpOnly: Native recording page/image hosts can change the pixel margin; PlaybackOptions retains the 12-pixel export margin. | Use recording raster presets for the supported layout, or set RecordingExportOptions.Padding in native artifact embedding. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Export.RecordingExportOptions.Timestamp` | CSharpOnly: Native asciicast serialization can override the optional header timestamp; the cmdlet does not add an export-time timestamp override. | Keep the recording's source metadata through Export-ConsoleRecording, or set Timestamp when a native caller creates an asciicast header. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Interactive.Choice.Tag` | CSharpOnly: Native selection hosts can attach metadata separate from Choice.Value. PowerShell selectors retain the chosen source object and return its value without a separate Tag projection. | Keep metadata on the original PowerShell choice object; native Choice.Tag remains available to a typed selection host. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Interactive.ConsoleAppOptions.Live` | CSharpOnly: A native app host can inject its full-screen live-session configuration; Show-ConsoleApp owns the session and maps input, capture, profile and theme through Interactive instead. | Use Show-ConsoleApp -InputSource/-Capture/-Profile/-Theme/-Mode; native ConsoleAppOptions.Live configures a custom session host. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Interactive.FormOptions.AfterSubmit` | CSharpOnly: A native full-screen form can run a MenuContext dashboard callback before leaving its screen. Read-ConsoleForm returns submitted answers and does not run another work callback inside that screen. | Read the form result, then invoke the requested PowerShell work or dashboard; native FormOptions.AfterSubmit retains in-screen composition. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Interactive.InteractiveOptions.Labels` | CSharpOnly: Native prompt hosts can inject a customized PromptLabels instance. PowerShell resolves the built-in catalogue from the active profile language rather than accepting a replacement label object. | Select CONSOLEMONSTER_LANGUAGE or the UI culture; set each question's Title/Description for its own wording. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Interactive.InteractiveOptions.LineConsole` | CSharpOnly: Native embeddings can inject line-oriented input/output devices. PSInteractive chooses the owning PowerShell host UI for Line/Accessible modes, including remoting and ISE. | Use the command's -Mode Line/Accessible; native InteractiveOptions.LineConsole can supply a custom device. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Interactive.InteractiveOptions.MaxInlineHeight` | CSharpOnly: Native prompt hosts can cap the inline screen independently of the detected terminal height. PowerShell keeps the shared automatic prompt-height policy. | Use supported PageSize/Height options on the specific input where exposed, or set MaxInlineHeight in a native prompt host. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Interactive.InteractiveOptions.NonInteractive` | CSharpOnly: Native hosts can explicitly disable prompting. PSInteractive detects the PowerShell process's NonInteractive state and maps it to Mode None instead of exposing a second Boolean. | Start PowerShell with -NonInteractive or choose the input command's -Mode None where supported. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Interactive.InteractiveOptions.Target` | CSharpOnly: Native callers can override one prompt's terminal target. PowerShell scopes its target through Terminal.Use and keeps input/capture overrides on the high-level app command. | Use Use-ConsoleTarget -Target for the scoped target, or Show-ConsoleApp -InputSource/-Capture for explicit app devices. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Interactive.KeyBinding.Group` | CSharpOnly: Native key-map hosts choose the heading under which a binding is listed; PowerShell menu/app commands use the shared host-generated action groups. | Use the input/menu defaults or New-ConsoleCommand -Hotkey/-Label for supported actions; configure this field on a native KeyBinding for a custom key map. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Interactive.KeyBinding.InFooter` | CSharpOnly: Native key-map hosts can suppress one binding in the footer while keeping it in the key map; PowerShell keeps the shared footer-selection policy. | Use the input/menu defaults or New-ConsoleCommand -Hotkey/-Label for supported actions; configure this field on a native KeyBinding for a custom key map. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Interactive.KeyBinding.KeyText` | CSharpOnly: Native bindings can replace the displayed chord text with a glyph or custom caption; PowerShell actions keep their actual Hotkey and generated key hints. | Use the input/menu defaults or New-ConsoleCommand -Hotkey/-Label for supported actions; configure this field on a native KeyBinding for a custom key map. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Interactive.KeyBinding.Order` | CSharpOnly: Native key-map hosts set the footer retention priority of a binding; PowerShell keeps the shared ordering of its generated input and command bindings. | Use the input/menu defaults or New-ConsoleCommand -Hotkey/-Label for supported actions; configure this field on a native KeyBinding for a custom key map. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Interactive.Menu.CommandProviders` | CSharpOnly: Native menu applications can add ICommandProvider implementations to discover palette actions. | `ConsoleMonster.Interactive.MenuOptions.ConfirmExit` | CSharpOnly: Native menu hosts may change the unsaved-change exit-confirmation policy; Show-ConsoleMenu deliberately retains the default confirmation. | Use Show-ConsoleMenu with its normal unsaved-change protection; set ConfirmExit in a native menu host when a different policy is required. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Interactive.MenuOptions.SidebarMinimumWidth` | CSharpOnly: Native menu hosts may tune the Shell sidebar breakpoint; Show-ConsoleMenu exposes the layout choice and keeps the 84-column breakpoint. | Use Show-ConsoleMenu -Layout Auto/Classic/Shell/Inline; native MenuOptions.SidebarMinimumWidth controls a custom breakpoint. |

| `ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveRunOptions.Session` | CSharpOnly: A native caller may supply an exclusive run session. Start-ConsoleRun creates its own session and selects host-safe capture/output before LiveRun fixes inline sizing, cancellation and its summary. | Use Start-ConsoleRun high-level live/progress/height options and Complete-ConsoleRun; native LiveRunOptions.Session is the embedding-host extension point. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.AutoRecordFolder` | CSharpOnly: Native hosts choose a separate automatic-recording directory. Invoke-ConsoleDashboard -AutoRecord uses the platform recording directory and does not expose a second storage path. | Use Invoke-ConsoleDashboard -RecordingPath for an explicit file, or -AutoRecord for the standard folder. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.AutoRecordMaxBytes` | CSharpOnly: Native hosts choose the automatic-recording retention budget. The PowerShell dashboard retains the bounded 50-MB default alongside its AutoRecord count. | Use Invoke-ConsoleDashboard -AutoRecord for retention count, or -RecordingPath for a caller-owned recording file. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.CaptureConsole` | CSharpOnly: Native session hosts decide whether to intercept Console.Out/Error. Start-ConsoleRun selects capture from the owning PowerShell host and uses a host queue when raw console capture would break that host. | Use Start-ConsoleRun/Invoke-ConsoleDashboard and their normal PowerShell stream routing; native sessions may set CaptureConsole explicitly. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.Culture` | CSharpOnly: Native hosts can pin one session's numeric/date culture. The PowerShell session keeps the detected profile culture instead of a per-session culture object. | Select the current culture or CONSOLEMONSTER_CULTURE for the host; native LiveSessionOptions.Culture can override one session. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.Discoverable` | CSharpOnly: Native hosts choose whether LiveSession.Current exposes a run to other operations. Start-ConsoleRun deliberately sets false so tracked work does not capture unrelated updates or prompts. | Update the returned run handle with Update-Console -Run; Invoke-ConsoleDashboard retains its normal discoverable dashboard scope. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.HandleCancelKey` | CSharpOnly: Native sessions choose whether to intercept Console.CancelKeyPress. Watch-Console disables this interception and uses PowerShell StopProcessing for Ctrl+C. | Use the high-level command's normal PowerShell cancellation; native LiveSessionOptions.HandleCancelKey configures console-host interception. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.LogTarget` | CSharpOnly: Native sessions may direct captured output to a particular log widget. LiveRun chooses its own dashboard log and ordinary dashboards discover the log target when this option is null. | Compose a log region in the dashboard or use Start-ConsoleRun's managed log; native hosts can select a LogTarget explicitly. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.NotifyOnFinish` | CSharpOnly: Native session hosts can enable the completion bell. PowerShell leaves the optional bell disabled rather than adding a command-level notification policy. | Use normal command completion and its final summary; native LiveSessionOptions.NotifyOnFinish enables a completion bell. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.Output` | CSharpOnly: Native hosts can lend an ITerminalOutput whose lifetime they own. The PowerShell dashboard selects a host queue/output implementation for jobs, remoting, transcripts and redirected output. | Use Use-ConsoleTarget for supported scoped output; the high-level live command owns its terminal-output lifecycle. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.Profile` | CSharpOnly: Native hosts may override a single session's terminal capabilities. PowerShell detects its current host and applies a plain host profile where direct terminal output is unsafe. | Use the detected host profile and high-level -NoLive; native LiveSessionOptions.Profile supplies a custom session profile. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.RecordingName` | CSharpOnly: Native hosts choose the automatic-recording filename prefix. Invoke-ConsoleDashboard deliberately uses dashboard for its automatic recordings. | Use Invoke-ConsoleDashboard -RecordingPath to name a file, or -AutoRecord for the dashboard-prefixed automatic series. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.RecordWriter` | CSharpOnly: Native hosts can lend an event-recording TextWriter that is flushed but left open. The PowerShell dashboard exposes an owned recording path, not a borrowed event sink. | Use Invoke-ConsoleDashboard -RecordingPath; native LiveSessionOptions.RecordWriter supports a caller-owned writer. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.ReplayDelay` | CSharpOnly: Native replay hosts can supply deterministic timing and cancellation handling. Show-ConsoleReplay exposes playback Speed and uses the normal replay delay implementation. | Use Show-ConsoleReplay -Speed/-PlaybackMode; native replay fixtures can provide LiveSessionOptions.ReplayDelay. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.StopOnCancellation` | CSharpOnly: Native hosts choose whether rendering stops immediately or drains until Stop. LiveRun deliberately sets false so completed worker results can reach the final summary. | Use Complete-ConsoleRun in finally and normal command cancellation; native sessions may choose their own drain policy. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.StopTimeout` | CSharpOnly: Native hosts set the render-thread join timeout. PowerShell commands retain the session's bounded two-second stop wait and own their finally/disposal path. | Use the high-level command's cancellation and cleanup; native LiveSessionOptions.StopTimeout tunes a custom host's render-thread join. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.StreamHeartbeat` | CSharpOnly: Native sessions tune append-only summary heartbeats. LiveRun disables the session heartbeat and owns its separate count/time progress triggers. | Use Start-ConsoleRun -ProgressEvery/-ProgressIntervalSeconds for run progress, or native StreamHeartbeat for a standalone session. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.StreamTimestamps` | CSharpOnly: Native hosts can override append-only narration timestamps. PowerShell retains automatic CI-profile detection instead of adding another timestamp switch to live commands. | Use the host's normal CI-aware narration; native LiveSessionOptions.StreamTimestamps forces the per-session timestamp policy. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.Target` | CSharpOnly: Native hosts can override one session's ITerminalTarget independently of the ambient target. PowerShell scopes the target and preserves high-level session ownership. | Use Use-ConsoleTarget -Target/-Path/-Writer around the command; native LiveSessionOptions.Target overrides a single session. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.TaskbarProgress` | CSharpOnly: Native hosts may disable the terminal/taskbar progress indicator. PowerShell retains the default automatic progress reporting and reset at session completion. | Use the normal live dashboard progress lifecycle; native LiveSessionOptions.TaskbarProgress changes the terminal-indicator policy. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.Theme` | CSharpOnly: Native hosts can override one session's ITheme independently of Terminal.Theme. The PowerShell live commands use the selected ambient theme. | Use Set-ConsoleTheme for the supported host theme; native LiveSessionOptions.Theme overrides one session. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Live.WatchOptions.Session` | CSharpOnly: Native watch hosts can supply an exclusive LiveSessionOptions instance. Watch-Console owns an inline session, final-state retention and cancellation through StopProcessing. | Use Watch-Console -NoLive/-PollIntervalSeconds/-Count; native WatchOptions.Session configures a custom watch host. |
| `ConsoleMonster.PowerShell.ConsoleDefaultOutputOptions.Force` | CSharpOnly: A native output adapter may force registered-view rendering outside direct console output. The installed PowerShell adapter supplies verified provenance and explicit Show commands select views directly. | Use Show-Console or Enable-ConsoleFormatting; custom native output hosts can configure ConsoleDefaultOutputOptions.Force. |
| `ConsoleMonster.PowerShell.ConsoleDefaultOutputOptions.HelpSink` | CSharpOnly: The native adapter supplies the actual help-producing PSCmdlet after checking its provenance. Accepting it from a script would not establish trusted help-output routing. | Use native Get-Help with ConsoleMonster help formatting enabled; a native host must provide its verified help sink. |
| `ConsoleMonster.PowerShell.ConsoleDefaultOutputOptions.Shim` | CSharpOnly: The native adapter marks its invocation as the installed default-output shim so only enabled formatting features run. This is adapter provenance, not a user formatting choice. | Use Enable-ConsoleFormatting -Include/-Exclude; the installed adapter supplies Shim internally. |
| `ConsoleMonster.PowerShell.ConsoleDefaultOutputOptions.TopLevel` | CSharpOnly: The native adapter establishes whether the sink belongs to a top-level submission before displaying automatic views and errors. A script flag cannot establish that pipeline provenance. | Use normal direct console output or an explicit Show command; the adapter determines TopLevel. |
| `ConsoleMonster.PowerShell.ConsoleDefaultOutputOptions.Transcript` | CSharpOnly: The native adapter preserves PowerShell's transcript routing and uses native Out-Default -Transcript when needed. Scripts do not choose this verified routing state. | Use PowerShell's normal Start-Transcript/Stop-Transcript lifecycle; the adapter supplies Transcript. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Replay.ReplayOptions.Interactive` | CSharpOnly: Native replay hosts may inject interactive devices, labels and targets. Show-ConsoleReplay builds host-aware PSInteractive options and supplies the owning host line console when needed. | Use Show-ConsoleReplay -PlaybackMode/-Paused and the normal host; native ReplayOptions.Interactive supports custom devices. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Replay.ReplayOptions.Session` | CSharpOnly: Native automatic-replay hosts may inject session output and deterministic delay. Show-ConsoleReplay owns its automatic-playback session and exposes playback controls rather than a nested session object. | Use Show-ConsoleReplay -PlaybackMode Automatic/-Speed/-Inline; native ReplayOptions.Session configures a custom replay host. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Sessions.SessionRecordingOptions.Folder` | CSharpOnly: Native recorders can change the directory used for automatically generated cast names. Invoke-ConsoleRecording exposes the exact recording file and retains the standard default directory when omitted. | Use Invoke-ConsoleRecording -RecordingPath to choose the complete cast path; native SessionRecordingOptions.Folder changes automatic naming location. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Views.ConsoleViewOptions.Alignment` | CSharpOnly: Native view builders can configure an embedded rule's alignment. Show-Console no longer owns the rule hierarchy/view job; the rule constructor retains its alignment contract. | Use New-ConsoleRule -Alignment and render the resulting widget, or configure ConsoleViewOptions.Alignment in native view code. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Views.ConsoleViewOptions.ChildrenProperty` | CSharpOnly: Native view builders can select a named hierarchy child member. Show-Console -View Tree now uses object inspection; explicit hierarchy construction belongs to New-ConsoleTree. | Use New-ConsoleTree -ChildrenProperty for a named child-member hierarchy, or Show-Console -View Tree for object inspection. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.FooterBar.FixedSlots` | CSharpOnly: Native app footers can reserve a slot for every command and shorten labels. Show-ConsoleApp -FooterHints builds the ordinary adaptive hint list. | Use -FooterHints for the supported hint layout; pass a configured FooterBar through Show-ConsoleApp -Footer for native fixed-slot composition. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.FooterBar.HintsSource` | CSharpOnly: Native app registries can supply render-time hints for the current focus/dialog. The PowerShell hint parameter is a concrete hint sequence and does not turn a scriptblock into a render-thread callback. | Use -FooterHints for fixed hints, or pass a typed FooterBar with a thread-safe native HintsSource through -Footer. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.FooterBar.Indent` | CSharpOnly: Native footer composition can change its first drawing column. The PowerShell built-in footer retains the standard one-cell inset. | Use Show-ConsoleApp -FooterHints for the standard inset, or pass a configured FooterBar through -Footer. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.FooterBar.KeepLast` | CSharpOnly: Native footers can preserve a final help/key-map hint when earlier hints overflow. The PowerShell footer keeps the standard adaptive list policy. | Choose the -FooterHints sequence for ordinary hints, or pass a configured FooterBar through -Footer for custom overflow retention. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.FooterBar.Message` | CSharpOnly: Native toast hosts can replace hints with a styled message line. PowerShell -FooterHints defines hints rather than a transient toast state. | Pass a configured FooterBar through Show-ConsoleApp -Footer for native message-state composition. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.FooterBar.Right` | CSharpOnly: Native footer composition can add a styled right-hand line independently of hints. The PowerShell hint shorthand owns only the hint sequence. | Pass a configured FooterBar through Show-ConsoleApp -Footer when a separate right-hand line is required. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.FooterBar.Segments` | CSharpOnly: Native footers can add right-hand linked/tinted metadata segments. The PowerShell hint shorthand does not construct FooterSegment records. | Pass a configured FooterBar through Show-ConsoleApp -Footer for native linked-segment composition. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.HeaderBar.Crumbs` | CSharpOnly: Native menu/form runners generate breadcrumb steps from their navigation stack; the Show-ConsoleApp header shorthand exposes title/subtitle rather than an independent breadcrumb collection. | Use menu/submenu navigation for generated breadcrumbs, or compose a typed HeaderBar in Show-ConsoleApp -Content. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.HeaderBar.Elapsed` | CSharpOnly: Native header hosts can pin the clock value instead of the render context clock. PowerShell dashboards use the session clock and do not expose a second header clock. | Use Invoke-ConsoleDashboard -Clock for a deterministic session clock, or compose a typed HeaderBar for an independent clock value. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.HeaderBar.HeaderRight` | CSharpOnly: Native grid/menu/form runners add contextual row/step captions to the header. The Show-ConsoleApp shorthand keeps its supported title/subtitle/detail/status fields. | Use Show-ConsoleApp -Detail/-Status for its status area, or compose a typed HeaderBar in -Content for independent right-hand text. |

## .NET host integrations

The PowerShell formatting, help and progress examples run inside a compiled PSCmdlet on its owning pipeline thread. The generic-host and ILogger examples configure .NET lifetimes; their PowerShell tab launches the same project. These options remain explicit C# integration settings.

| Package and C# member | PowerShell route and reason |
